senses.gloss: māṣa (EI 21, 25, 30, 33; CII 4), according to the Kṛtyakalpataru (Vyavahāra-kāṇḍa, ed. K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar, p. 125), a gold coin as opposed to silver māṣaka; name of a weight; name of a coin; 5 ratis in weight; sometimes regarded as 10 ratis in weight and as equal to (1/4) of a śāna. See JNSI, Vol. XVI, p. 41. It was sometimes regarded as (1/20) of a paṇa of 100 ratis (ibid., Vol. XV, p. 143). Cf. māṣaka, ādya-māṣa.

māṣa , name of a weight or a coin weighing 5 ratis originally; later regarded as 10 ratis in weight; (1/4) of a śāna and (1/8) of a śatamāna; sometimes regarded as (1/20) of a paṇa of 100 ratis (i. e. 5 ratis); a gold coin (as opposed to the silver māṣaka) according to the Kṛtyakalpataru; cf. ādya-māṣa, māḍa.
māṣaka (IE 8-8), name of a coin; cf. māṣa and dināri-māṣaka; mentioned as a silver coin (K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar, Kṛtyakalpataru, Vyavahāra-kāṇḍa, p. 125).
māṣaka , same as māṣa; according to the Kṛtyakalpataru, a silver coin as opposed to the gold māṣa
māsārdha (IE 7-1-2), used to indicate ‘six’; cf. māsa, ‘twelve’; also pakṣa, ‘two’.
Māśu (Chamba), one enjoying land, who does not pay rent or tax but renders service; e. g., a carpenter, etc.
